evidence_method: Two structured subjective passes over the exact 16 approved PNG captures; runtime replay verifies every screenshot byte against its approved SHA-256 before returning the assessments.

assessments.summary: Current establishes clear page titles, product imagery, and commerce actions.
assessments.alternate_summary: Current keeps core titles, media, and purchase actions legible and ordered.
assessments.rationale: The hero and PDP lead clearly, while supporting pages remain conventional and easy to scan.

assessments.summary: Editorial creates clear image-led focal points and deliberate title hierarchy.
assessments.alternate_summary: Editorial consistently gives media and page titles an intentional first-read position.
assessments.rationale: Asymmetric collection and PDP layouts create a stronger editorial sequence without obscuring commerce actions.

assessments.summary: Empty titled regions and repeated signup areas interrupt otherwise consistent rhythm.
assessments.alternate_summary: Rhythm loses coherence where empty headings and duplicate signup surfaces create dead zones.
assessments.rationale: Large gaps can be intentional, but visible headings without content and consecutive newsletter areas do not communicate a deliberate editorial pause.

assessments.summary: Editorial uses generous asymmetry intentionally, but empty titled sections still create unfinished pauses.
assessments.alternate_summary: Editorial whitespace reads as deliberate until unsupported headings create visibly incomplete intervals.
assessments.rationale: The product layouts show controlled breathing room; empty collection and PDP modules weaken that control.

assessments.summary: Both homepages give authoritative product media appropriate visual dominance.
assessments.alternate_summary: The approved snowboard imagery remains the primary visual anchor in both homepage directions.
assessments.rationale: Image scale, unobstructed product visibility, and concise text overlays support the image-led intent.

assessments.summary: The approved D1 overflow materially disrupts the mobile composition.
assessments.alternate_summary: Mobile hierarchy is visually compromised by the already-authoritative D1 containment failure.
assessments.rationale: This assessment records design impact only; D1 remains authoritative for the 390px viewport and 657px document geometry.

assessments.summary: Editorial preserves the hero priority and converts product discovery into a contained horizontal sequence.
assessments.alternate_summary: Editorial mobile keeps the hero dominant and adapts discovery without widening the page.
assessments.rationale: The 390px capture remains contained and the partially visible next card communicates deliberate continuation.

assessments.summary: Current provides a conventional, scan-friendly product grid with clear price and filter hierarchy.
assessments.alternate_summary: Current collection discovery is familiar and legible across desktop and mobile.
assessments.rationale: The uniform cards support comparison, though they provide little merchandising emphasis among products.

assessments.summary: Editorial creates a clear featured-first merchandising rhythm while preserving product facts.
assessments.alternate_summary: Editorial distinguishes one lead product and sequences the remaining catalog without losing scanability.
assessments.rationale: Scale contrast and numbering make discovery materially different from the uniform Current grid.

assessments.summary: The short collection title breaks inside a word in the narrow editorial title column.
assessments.alternate_summary: The desktop banner forces “Hydrogen” into an awkward mid-word wrap despite ample page width.
assessments.rationale: Large editorial scale is appropriate, but the constrained measure produces a visibly unintended reading break.

assessments.summary: Current presents media, title, price, quantity, and purchase actions in a clear decision sequence.
assessments.alternate_summary: Current maintains a direct and legible buying-information progression on both viewports.
assessments.rationale: Primary purchase actions are prominent and supporting sections follow the main product decision area.

assessments.summary: Editorial strengthens title and media composition without reducing purchase-action clarity.
assessments.alternate_summary: Editorial gives the product study more character while retaining a clear buying path.
assessments.rationale: The desktop split is materially distinct; mobile retains title, price, quantity, and actions in a reliable order.

assessments.summary: Current separates brand, primary links, and utilities clearly.
assessments.alternate_summary: Current header hierarchy remains understandable and restrained across routes.
assessments.rationale: Desktop distribution is conventional and mobile prioritizes menu, brand, and core utilities.

assessments.summary: Editorial centers brand identity and gives navigation a deliberate secondary line on desktop.
assessments.alternate_summary: Editorial creates a recognizable centered brand-and-navigation hierarchy without hiding utilities.
assessments.rationale: The header is materially differentiated on desktop while mobile remains compact and familiar.

assessments.summary: No approved Design DNA payload is present in the controlled comparison provenance.
assessments.alternate_summary: Design DNA coherence cannot be judged because the fixture exposes no approved DNA revision payload.
assessments.rationale: The evaluator must not infer Design DNA from appearance, preset identity, or architecture labels.

assessments.summary: Desktop hierarchy, discovery, header, and PDP composition are materially distinct.
assessments.alternate_summary: The two profiles produce clearly different desktop reading order and merchandising structure.
assessments.rationale: Editorial uses centered navigation, asymmetric featured products, and a product-study layout rather than only cosmetic variation.

assessments.summary: Homepage and collection adapt distinctly, while the two PDPs converge strongly on mobile.
assessments.alternate_summary: Mobile differentiation is clear in discovery surfaces but limited in the product purchase composition.
assessments.rationale: Commerce ordering remains appropriately stable, yet Editorial mobile PDP expresses less architectural distinction than its desktop counterpart.

assessments.summary: Cart body similarity is intentional because both profiles select the Current cart family.
assessments.alternate_summary: The shared cart presentation matches registered family provenance and is not a differentiation defect.
assessments.rationale: Only the architecture-specific header changes; the cart family is explicitly shared by design.

assessments.summary: Visible section headings without supporting content make collection and PDP flows appear unfinished.
assessments.alternate_summary: Unsupported headings create incomplete modules across both profiles and both viewports.
assessments.rationale: Minimal merchant content should result in truthful omission rather than large titled empty regions.

assessments.summary: The desktop footer brand wraps its final letter onto an isolated line.
assessments.alternate_summary: A repeated orphaned final letter in the desktop footer reads as an unfinished detail.
assessments.rationale: The issue repeats across profiles and routes, indicating shared presentation handling rather than merchant content quality.

assessments.summary: A page newsletter immediately followed by a second footer newsletter repeats the same action without hierarchy.
assessments.alternate_summary: Two adjacent newsletter signup surfaces dilute rather than reinforce the homepage ending.
assessments.rationale: The repetition is present in both architectures and is not required by limited merchant content.

assessments.summary: Strong primary layouts are undermined by repeated incomplete supporting modules and footer wrapping.
assessments.alternate_summary: The architecture work is coherent, but shared empty modules and footer details prevent a fully finished impression.
assessments.rationale: These concerns are visible across multiple routes and cannot be explained solely by one weak merchant asset.

findings.diagnosis: The authoritative D1 root overflow makes Current mobile Homepage content appear cropped and off-canvas; D2 records design impact without re-measuring or contradicting D1 geometry.
findings.alternate_diagnosis: Current mobile Homepage loses compositional clarity because of the already-approved D1 containment defect; this is impact evidence, not a second geometry finding.

findings.diagnosis: Collection and PDP captures expose headings for unsupported modules with no useful content, creating unfinished page flow instead of omission-first behavior.
findings.alternate_diagnosis: Empty titled collection and product modules interrupt both architectures and should be treated as composition handling, not fabricated or missing merchant copy.

findings.diagnosis: Homepage ends with two adjacent newsletter signup surfaces, weakening CTA hierarchy in both profiles.
findings.alternate_diagnosis: Repeated page and footer newsletter forms create redundant closing actions across both homepage directions.

findings.diagnosis: The shared desktop footer wraps the final letter of the brand name onto an isolated line across routes.
findings.alternate_diagnosis: A repeated one-letter brand wrap in the desktop footer creates a visible unfinished detail.

findings.diagnosis: Editorial desktop Collection constrains the short title enough to split “Hydrogen” inside the word, reducing polish and readability.
findings.alternate_diagnosis: The editorial title column produces an awkward mid-word break for a short authoritative collection name.

findings.diagnosis: Editorial mobile PDP converges closely with Current after the title, limiting architecture differentiation while retaining a sound purchase flow.
findings.alternate_diagnosis: The product purchase sequence is appropriately stable, but Editorial expresses little distinct mobile structure beyond its label and title treatment.
findings.architecture_intent: editorial product study compared with Current
